CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain after injury at trampoline park.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while at a trampoline park with his wife. He heard a distinct pop/snap when he landed on the trampoline and experienced immediate onset of pain on the lateral aspect of the right knee. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park. He has not engaged in regular exercise recently. Since the injury, he has not tried formal treatment aside from elevation and acetaminophen, which provided minimal relief. He reports being able to bear weight but notes a slight limp when ambulating.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies recent illness or other systemic symptoms. Reports pain with knee movement but denies fever, chills, or constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented in conversation.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in conversation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is sedentary with inconsistent exercise regimen. Denies regular workout routine. Reports reluctance to seek medical care. Lives with wife.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at 180/80 mmHg.
General: Alert and oriented.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs appreciated.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal - Right knee: Ecchymosis and edema noted over lateral aspect. Tenderness to palpation on lateral aspect; no tenderness on medial aspect. Good range of motion but with pain on some movements. No effusion noted. Gait: Slight limp observed.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee lateral ligament strain: Start meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Consider further imaging if pain persists. Advised that this injury typically heals on its own.
2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram. Anticipate possible medication modification depending on blood pressure response and echocardiogram results.
3. Diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c and lipid panel to assess long-term glycemic control and assess need for medication adjustment.
